question: A finance team's project instructions state: "never give a figure without naming the report it came from". Which addition would most improve this instruction?
options: A) Adding the rule a second time at the end of the instructions, so it is less likely to be overlooked.
B) Adding why the rule exists, so Claude can apply the same care to cases the rule did not anticipate.
C) Adding an instruction to repeat the rule at the top of every answer, so readers can see it was followed.
D) Adding the names of the three people who approved the rule, so Claude knows the rule is authoritative.
correct_answers: B) Adding why the rule exists, so Claude can apply the same care to cases the rule did not anticipate.
explanations: Duplication does not clarify the rule and lengthens the instructions for no benefit.
Correct. Stating the reason lets the intent generalise to situations the literal wording never covered.
Restating the rule in the output adds noise without improving whether it is actually followed.
Approval provenance changes nothing about how the rule is applied to an answer.
